answer: Epoch behavior match rule. Each identity submits an epoch summary; its fingerprint is held in a vault and compared with the prior two epochs, accepted only if similarity exceeds a threshold. Fresh aliases lack history, so an attacker must run each sybil identity through three distinct epochs of consistent activity. A drifting dune of action mix fails. Passing identities get a violet continuity mark; per identity, the attacker pays fees and storage for three epochs plus lost time.
